_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Teaches controlled classification systems for categories, facets, browse taxonomies, SKOS broader/narrower links,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "our skill categories are drifting: some are by domain, some by activity, and some by tool - how should the taxonomy be redesigned?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the taxonomy-design skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is taxonomy-design the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes taxonomy-design as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against skill-infrastructure, information-architecture, context-graph
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the taxonomy-design workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore taxonomy-design
Does not route to skill-infrastructure, information-architecture, context-graph when the taxonomy-design scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "define OWL class restrictions and property domains for this knowledge base"
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should taxonomy-design be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside taxonomy-design's ownership
Routes the work to skill-infrastructure or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying taxonomy-design terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply taxonomy-design as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if taxonomy-design has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim taxonomy-design should own the request
Does not use taxonomy-design's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
